newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate approves Albright as secretary of state.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate approves Albright as secretary of state.

text.p: The Senate on Wednesday confirmed Madeleine Albright as U.S. secretary of state, the first woman to hold the post.
Albright, who has served as President Bill Clinton's ambassador to the United Nations, was the first new member of Clinton's second-term Cabinet to win approval.

Albright, 59, who succeeds Warren Christopher, was approved by a vote of 99-0. She was born in Prague and emigrated to the United States with her family at the age of 11 after a communist coup in her native Czechoslovakia.

Sen. Jesse Helms, a North Carolina Republican who chairs the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, supported Albright's nomination but faulted Clinton's foreign policy over the past four years, which he said had given "a message of weakened resolve around the world."

Helms said that "we'll be watching her closely" to see if the administration had learned from the past "disasters", which he said included U.S. involvement in Somalia and Haiti. Helms said that he would reintroduce a plan to reorganize the State Department, promising it would save $1 billion a year.
The Senate voted on Albright as the Armed Services Committee prepared to approve Clinton's nominee for defense secretary, former Republican Senator William Cohen of Maine.
